adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:90 — group.users.delete(user_id)` calls `association.find(id)` first, so removing a user who is not (or is no longer) a member raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound -> 404; a double-clicked remove X or a stale member list now errors where the deleted "succeeds silently when removing non-members" spec guaranteed a no-op.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `remove_member` action, the code does `group.users.delete(user_id)` with a numeric id. In Rails, `collection.delete(id)` does not typically perform an `association.find(id)` constrained to the association (which would raise if the record isn’t currently associated). It either deletes join rows directly (common for `has_many :through`/HABTM) or, if it does load a record, it would be `User.find(user_id)` (raising only if the user record doesn’t exist at all), not “not a member”. Therefore the specific claim that removing a non-member/stale membership will raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound` is not verifiable from this diff and is likely a mischaracterization of `delete` semantics.

Using the association `delete` bypasses model-level removal logic (and, in Rails, `delete` on associations generally does not instantiate/destroy join records, so callbacks/counter-cache-style bookkeeping on the join model or in `Group#remove` will not run). Thus it’s a real correctness risk introduced by the diff: removals may not properly maintain derived fields like `user_count`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:72 — Unknown/typo'd usernames are silently skipped and the endpoint still returns success_json, so an admin adding "bob,bbo" gets "success" with one member added and no indication which name failed; the spec that pinned this behavior was deleted.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:71 — The usernames string is unbounded and each name costs a find_by_username plus an exists? plus an insert, so one request with tens of thousands of names produces an unbounded query storm and a half-applied group.

There is no bound/limit on the size of the `usernames` string or number of entries, and it performs at least one DB lookup (`find_by_username`) per username. adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:34 — The incremental `PATCH /admin/groups/:id` `changes:{add,delete}` API is deleted, but `resources :groups` still routes PATCH to `update`, so legacy clients get 200 OK while their membership edits are silently discarded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:38 — update` unconditionally assigns `visible = params[:visible] == "true"`, so legacy PATCH/partial-update callers that omit `visible` now silently flip the group to hidden.

If a legacy caller sends a PATCH/partial update without `visible` (previously handled by `update_patch`, which didn’t touch `visible`), `params[:visible]` will be nil and the expression evaluates to false, flipping `visible` off. adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:24 — Admin create/update params moved from nested `group:{...}` to top-level, so any client still sending `group[name]`/`group[visible]` now creates a blank-named group or no-ops the rename while still clobbering `visible`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:25 — create` ignores `alias_level` even though `Discourse.Group#asJSON` sends it and `update` honors it, so the alias level chosen for a new group in app/assets/javascripts/admin/templates/group.hbs:43 is dropped.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:28 — create` returns a serialized `basic_group` payload while `update` returns bare `success_json`, an inconsistent response contract for the same resource.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show that `Admin::GroupsController#create` renders a serialized `BasicGroupSerializer` payload, while `#update` renders `success_json`. adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both the golden comment and the candidate issue point out the same underlying problem: the remove_member controller spec uses an XHR PUT request, but the Rails route is defined to use DELETE for groups#remove_member, so the test's HTTP verb doesn't match the routing configuration.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:98 — Coverage dropped without replacement: silent skip of unknown usernames, removing a non-member, and alias_level/visible on update are no longer tested

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes several specs under the old `.update` incremental PATCH behavior (adds/removes, including adding non-existent users and removing non-members) and replaces them with narrower `.add_members` tests that only cover adding valid users and blocking automatic groups. It also replaces broader update coverage with a single test that only asserts `visible` changes and that `name` is ignored for an automatic group; there is no new test asserting `alias_level` behavior, nor tests for the previously covered “succeeds silently when adding non-existent users” / “succeeds silently when removing non-members” cases. So the finding about coverage dropping without replacement is directly verifiable in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22 — User-controlled `limit` has no upper clamp on this anonymous-accessible endpoint, so `?limit=10000000` against an automatic group (e.g. trust_level_0 = every user) fetches and serializes the entire membership in one request.

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff sets `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and directly passes it to `group.users...limit(limit)` with no maximum cap. This endpoint is in the non-admin `groups_controller.rb` and is guarded only by `guardian.ensure_can_see!(group)`, so for any group a user can see (including large/automatic groups), a request like `?limit=10000000` can trigger a very large DB result set and serialization work in one response. The diff also removed the prior special-casing for automatic groups and now applies the user-controlled `limit` to all groups, making the unbounded parameter more broadly exploitable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:25 — group.users.count` adds a full COUNT(*) over the group_users/users join on every single page request, doubling DB work per page instead of reading the already-serialized denormalized `user_count`.

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff introduces `total = group.users.count` before loading the paginated `members` relation. This will issue an extra `COUNT(*)` query on the `group.users` association for every members request, in addition to the query that fetches the actual page of users. Since the `Group` model already has a `user_count` attribute (used elsewhere/serialized) and the controller has the `group` record loaded, using `group.user_count` would avoid that additional DB hit, so the finding describes a real performance regression introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:26 — order(:username_lower)` spans the join (group_id on group_users, username_lower on users) so no index can satisfy it, forcing a sort of the group's whole membership per page, and OFFSET is uncapped so deep pages generate and discard everything before them.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `GroupsController#members` to always paginate and to `order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)`. While a very large `offset` can indeed be inefficient in general, the proposed finding’s stronger claim that `order(:username_lower)` “spans the join” such that “no index can satisfy it” and that it “forces a sort of the group’s whole membership per page” cannot be verified from the diff (it depends on the DB schema/indexes and query plan, which aren’t shown). The code also doesn’t introduce an obvious correctness or security bug; it’s at most a speculative performance concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:72 — User.find_by_username` inside the loop is a classic N+1 (one SELECT per username) where a single `User.where(username_lower: names)` would do.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the diff introduces `usernames.split(",").each` and calls `User.find_by_username(username)` inside the loop. That issues one database query per username provided, which is a verifiable per-item query pattern that can be replaced with a single `WHERE ... IN (...)` query (e.g., fetching all users up front) to avoid unnecessary round-trips when many usernames are submitted.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:71 — The comma-separated `usernames` list is iterated with no cap on its length, so one request can tie up a worker for an unbounded number of sequential lookups and per-user inserts.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the code does `usernames.split(",").each` and for each entry performs `User.find_by_username` and `group.add(user)`. There is no application-level limit on how many usernames can be supplied in the `usernames` param, so a single request can trigger an arbitrarily large number of sequential DB lookups and membership inserts (bounded only by external request-size limits, not by this code). This is a verifiable performance/DoS risk introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:47 — removeMember` triggers a full `findMembers()` refetch (page query + server COUNT) after every single removal, so clearing N members costs 2N requests and N COUNTs instead of a local splice.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Discourse.Group#removeMember` issues a DELETE to `/admin/groups/:id/members.json` and then unconditionally calls `self.findMembers()` in the `.then(...)` handler. `findMembers()` performs an additional AJAX GET to `/groups/:name/members.json` with pagination and, per `GroupsController#members`, the server computes `total = group.users.count` on every call. Therefore, removing N members one-by-one will reliably produce ~2N client requests (N DELETEs + N GET refreshes) and N server COUNTs, rather than updating the local `members` array.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:4 — Group.order(:name)` is rendered with no limit or pagination, serializing every group on the site into one response.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#index`, the code does indeed build `groups = Group.order(:name)` and then `render_serialized(groups, BasicGroupSerializer)` without any explicit `limit`/pagination. However, this behavior is not introduced by the diff (the method already returned all groups; the diff only changes `ilike` to `ILIKE` and formatting), and the claim that it is a defect is largely a performance concern/speculation without evidence in the diff that pagination is required or expected for this admin endpoint.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/routes/admin_group_route.js:13 — afterModel replaced by fire-and-forget model.findMembers(), so a failed fetch is an unhandled rejection and the member list silently renders empty with no loading state

adjudication.rationale: In `admin_group_route.js`, the previous `afterModel` hook returned `model.findMembers().then(...)`, which meant the route transition was aware of the async fetch and a rejection could be handled via Ember’s route error mechanisms. The new `setupController` does `model.findMembers();` without returning the promise or attaching a `.catch`, so if the underlying `Discourse.ajax(...)` in `Group#findMembers` rejects, it becomes an unhandled rejection and the UI has no built-in error/loading handling in this path. Also, since the template renders `{{each member in members}}` (proxied from `model.members`), it will be empty/undefined until the async call resolves, with no explicit loading state added in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6:11 — Same un-awaited model.findMembers() in setupController: fetch errors are never surfaced and the page stays permanently blank

adjudication.rationale: In the new `group-members` route, `setupController(controller, model)` calls `model.findMembers();` but does not return/await the promise. Previously, `afterModel` returned the `findMembers()` promise, so a failure would reject the transition and bubble through Ember’s route error handling. With the new code, if the AJAX call fails, the rejection is not propagated via the route lifecycle (and may become an unhandled rejection), so fetch errors won’t be surfaced the same way and `members` may never be set, leaving the members list empty. The “permanently blank” aspect is conditional on request failure (on success it should re-render when `members` is set).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:21 — findMembers returns undefined for an empty name instead of a resolved promise, so any caller chaining .then() throws a TypeError

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Discourse.Group#findMembers` was changed to `return;` when the group name is empty, which would indeed make `findMembers().then(...)` throw a TypeError. However, all call sites modified in this diff (admin_group_route, group-members route, and controller actions) now call `model.findMembers()` without chaining `.then()`, and the previous `.then()`-based usages were removed. Since no remaining caller in the provided diff chains `.then()`, the claimed breakage is not verifiable from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:51 — addMembers has no rejection handler, so a 422/403 from the server (automatic group, bad usernames) is silently swallowed with no UI feedback

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `addMembers` returns the `Discourse.ajax(...).then(...)` promise without a rejection handler, but that does not mean errors are “silently swallowed”: the rejection will propagate to the caller. The caller (`admin-group` controller action `addMembers`) also doesn’t attach a handler, but whether that results in “no UI feedback” depends on global `Discourse.ajax` error handling (not shown in this diff), so it’s not verifiable here. Also, the UI prevents calling `addMembers` for automatic groups (`{{#unless automatic}}`), and the server’s `add_members` path does not 422 on “bad usernames” (it ignores unknown users), weakening the specific 422/403 scenario claimed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:40 — removeMember has no rejection handler, so a failed DELETE leaves the member displayed and reports nothing to the admin

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `removeMember` does return the `Discourse.ajax(...).then(...)` promise without a `.catch`/rejection handler, and the controller action that calls it also doesn’t attach error handling. However, the finding’s claimed impact (“failed DELETE leaves the member displayed and reports nothing to the admin”) isn’t a verifiable defect from this diff alone: if the DELETE fails, keeping the member displayed is the correct state (the server didn’t remove them), and whether the admin sees an error depends on global AJAX error handling outside this diff. The diff does not prove that failures are silent.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:47 — The inner self.findMembers() refresh is not returned, so the outer promise resolves before the reload finishes and reload failures go unhandled

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js, both removeMember and addMembers do `return Discourse.ajax(...).then(function() { self.findMembers(); });`. Because the `then` callback does not `return self.findMembers()`, the promise returned by removeMember/addMembers resolves immediately after the DELETE/PUT succeeds, without waiting for the member list reload to finish. Any failure in `findMembers()` will also not be chained/handled by the returned promise. This is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:58 — Same un-returned inner self.findMembers() in addMembers: caller sees success before the list is refreshed and refresh errors are lost

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js, addMembers returns the promise from Discourse.ajax(...).then(...), but inside the then-callback it calls self.findMembers() without returning it. That means the promise returned by addMembers resolves as soon as the PUT completes, not after the members list refresh completes. Any rejection/errors from findMembers() would also not propagate to the addMembers() caller. This behavior is directly verifiable in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:59 — Missing semicolon after the addMembers .then(...) block relies on ASI and is fragile under asset concatenation/minification

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `addMembers` ends with `return Discourse.ajax(...).then(function() { ... })` followed immediately by `},` (end of the function property in an object literal). The lack of a semicolon after the `then(...)` call is valid JavaScript due to ASI, and because the next token is `},` (not `(`, `[`, `+`, etc.), it does not create a concatenation/minification hazard. This is a style nit, not a verifiable defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:23 — Offset is clamped against the stale user_count, so removing the last member of the final page re-requests an out-of-range offset and renders an empty page with no correction

adjudication.rationale: Real issue. In `Discourse.Group.findMembers`, the requested `offset` is clamped with `Math.min(this.get("user_count"), ...)`. That allows `offset == user_count`, which is already out-of-range (returns an empty page). After deleting the last member on the last page, `removeMember` calls `self.findMembers()` while `user_count` on the model is still the old total, so the clamp won’t reduce `offset` to a valid last-page offset. The request can be made with an offset past the new end of the list and the model is then updated with empty `members` and no corrective offset adjustment, leaving the UI on an empty page.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:29 — next does not guard against an in-flight findMembers, so double-clicking issues overlapping requests whose out-of-order responses leave offset and members inconsistent

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `admin-group.js.es6`, the `next` action updates `group.offset` and immediately calls `group.findMembers()` with no debounce/disable/in-flight guard. In `discourse/models/group.js`, `findMembers()` performs an async AJAX call and, on completion, unconditionally `setProperties({ user_count, limit, offset, members })` from the response. If a user double-clicks “next”, two requests with different offsets can be in flight; if the earlier request resolves after the later one, it will overwrite `offset` and `members` with stale data (and thus `currentPage/showingLast` too), leaving UI state inconsistent with the most recent click.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:40 — previous has the same missing in-flight guard and can interleave paged responses

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds async pagination actions `next` and `previous` in `admin-group.js.es6` that update `model.offset` and immediately call `group.findMembers()`, which performs an AJAX request and, when it resolves, overwrites `user_count/limit/offset/members` on the model. There is no in-flight/loading guard (e.g., disabling the controls while a request is pending) or request-cancellation/tokening to ensure only the latest response applies. If an admin clicks next/previous quickly, multiple requests can be outstanding and may resolve out of order, causing a stale response to overwrite the members list/offset for the most recent page selection. The only guards present (`showingFirst/showingLast`) prevent going past bounds, not interleaving responses.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:64 — addMembers discards the returned promise: no error surfacing, no button disable, and the input is never cleared (TODO line 62) so a second click resubmits the same usernames

adjudication.rationale: In admin-group.js.es6 the addMembers action calls `this.get("model").addMembers(this.get("usernames"));` and does not return the promise that `Group#addMembers` returns (it returns the `Discourse.ajax(...).then(...)` chain). The action also leaves `usernames` unchanged; the comment `// TODO: should clear the input` confirms the input is not cleared. As a result, after a successful add, the same usernames remain in the selector and a second click will re-submit the same usernames again. There is also no local state change (e.g., disabling the button) tied to the in-flight promise in this action.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:56 — removeMember discards the promise returned by model.removeMember, so a rejected DELETE is silently ignored

app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:4 — usernames is never reset in the route setupController, so text typed on this singleton controller persists across groups and can be added to the wrong group

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `admin-group.js.es6` changes `usernames` from a computed property (derived from `members`) to a plain mutable property (`usernames: null`). The `AdminGroupRoute#setupController` was also changed to only set the model and call `model.findMembers()`, and it no longer sets any member-related state nor resets `usernames`. In Ember, route controllers are singletons reused across transitions for the same route, so a text value bound to `usernames` in `admin/templates/group.hbs` (the `{{user-selector usernames=usernames ...}}`) can persist when switching between different group models, leading to adding the previously typed usernames to the newly selected group unless explicitly cleared (e.g., via `resetController`/manual reset in `setupController`). This persistence risk is directly implied by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/group/members.hbs:6 — Public members list is now capped at the model default limit of 50 with no pagination controls, so members past the first page are silently unreachable

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `GroupsController#members` to always apply `limit` (default 50) and `offset`, returning only a page of members plus meta. On the client, `group-members` route now sets the controller model to the `group` and calls `model.findMembers()`, which requests `/groups/<name>/members.json` with `limit`/`offset` and stores the results in `group.members`. The public template `discourse/templates/group/members.hbs` was updated to iterate `{{#each m in members}}`, but no pagination UI or actions (next/previous) are added anywhere for the public members page (pagination controls were only added in the *admin* group template/controller). As a result, only the first page (50 members by default) is reachable from the public members list.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:71 — add_members silently skips usernames that do not resolve to a user yet still returns success_json, so partial failures are invisible to the caller

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the code iterates `usernames.split(",")` and only adds a user if `User.find_by_username(username)` returns a record; nonexistent usernames are simply ignored. Regardless of whether some (or all) usernames were skipped, it proceeds to `group.save` and returns `success_json` on save. This makes partial (or total) failures to add requested usernames invisible to the caller, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:71 — usernames.split(",") raises NoMethodError (500) when usernames is submitted as an array or hash instead of a string

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the diff sets `usernames = params.require(:usernames)` and immediately calls `usernames.split(",")`. `params.require` does not coerce types; if a client submits `usernames[]=` (array) or a nested structure, `usernames` will be an `Array`/`Hash`, which does not implement `split`, causing a `NoMethodError` and a 500. The code has no guard/coercion to prevent this.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:71 — The per-user group.add loop is not wrapped in a transaction, so a mid-loop failure leaves the group partially updated

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the code iterates `usernames.split(",")` and calls `group.add(user)` for each found user, then calls `group.save`. The proposed issue (“mid-loop failure leaves partially updated group”) is speculative: the diff doesn’t show that `group.add` can raise or fail mid-loop, nor that the operation is intended to be atomic/all-or-nothing. Given the method already silently skips unknown users, partial success appears acceptable and no concrete failure path is verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:67 — params.require(:usernames) raises ActionController::ParameterMissing on a blank value, returning a non-JSON error body the client cannot parse

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, `usernames = params.require(:usernames)` will indeed raise `ActionController::ParameterMissing` if the `usernames` key is absent (and in many Rails versions if it’s blank/""), *before* the controller can render `success_json`/`render_json_error`. However, the diff also changes the client to guard against empty usernames (`if (Em.isEmpty(this.get("usernames"))) { return; }`), so the new UI won’t normally trigger this. The claim that this would return a “non-JSON error body the client cannot parse” is not verifiable from the diff (it depends on global exception handling in the app), and using `require` to enforce a mandatory param is not inherently a defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:90 — group.users.delete removes the membership row immediately, so if the following group.save fails the caller gets an error while the deletion is already committed

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`, the code does `group.users.delete(user_id)` and only then checks `if group.save ... else ...`. In Rails, `association.delete` removes the join row immediately (it issues SQL right away) and is not contingent on calling `group.save`. Therefore, if `group.save` returns false (validations/callbacks fail, or the record is otherwise invalid), the action will respond with an error even though the membership deletion has already been committed, with no rollback/transaction in place. This is a real correctness/consistency issue introduced by the shown code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22 — limit is taken unbounded from params, letting a client request an arbitrarily large page and force an expensive query and serialization

adjudication.rationale: In app/controllers/groups_controller.rb#members the code sets `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and then uses it directly in `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)` and serializes the resulting users. There is no max cap or validation on `params[:limit]`, so a client can request an arbitrarily large limit, potentially causing an expensive query and large JSON serialization.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22 — Public members endpoint accepts an uncapped user-controlled limit, so an anonymous caller can dump a whole automatic group (e.g. trust_level_0 = every user) in one request

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff sets `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and then directly applies it to the query: `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)`. There is no upper bound/clamping on `limit`, so a caller can request an arbitrarily large number of members in one request. The endpoint is gated by `guardian.ensure_can_see!(group)`, so whether an *anonymous* caller can dump a specific automatic group depends on group visibility/permissions, but the uncapped, user-controlled `limit` described in the finding is verifiably present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:26 — Negative limit/offset params are passed straight to the query, producing LIMIT -1 / OFFSET -1 and an unrescued PG StatementInvalid 500 on a public endpoint

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members` the diff sets `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` and then directly calls `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)`. There is no validation/clamping to ensure `limit`/`offset` are non-negative. A request with `offset=-1` will pass a negative OFFSET through to SQL, which PostgreSQL rejects (raising `PG::InvalidParameterValue` / `ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid`), resulting in an unhandled 500 on this non-admin endpoint (`/groups/:group_id/members.json`). The JS caller clamps offset, but the controller still accepts arbitrary params, so the issue is verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:71 — params.require(:usernames) is never type-checked, so usernames[]=a makes .split raise NoMethodError and return a 500 instead of a 400

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the code does `usernames = params.require(:usernames)` and then immediately calls `usernames.split(",")`. Rails will permit `usernames` to be an Array when the request is shaped like `usernames[]=a&usernames[]=b` (or JSON array). In that case `params.require(:usernames)` returns an Array, and `Array#split` does not exist, causing a `NoMethodError` and a 500 response. There is no type coercion/validation in the diff to prevent this.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:38 — update unconditionally rewrites visible from params, so any request omitting visible silently sets it false and flips the group's guardian visibility

adjudication.rationale: In the new `Admin::GroupsController#update`, the code does `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` with no guard for presence. In Rails, when `params[:visible]` is omitted it is `nil`, and `nil == "true"` evaluates to `false`, so `visible` will be overwritten to `false` on any update request that doesn’t include `visible`. This is a concrete behavior directly implied by the diff and can unintentionally flip group visibility.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:37 — update has no can_not_modify_automatic guard, so alias_level/visible are still mutable on automatic groups unlike destroy/add_members/remove_member

adjudication.rationale: In the new `Admin::GroupsController#update`, automatic groups are still allowed to change `alias_level` and `visible` while only `name` changes are blocked (`group.name = ... if ... && !group.automatic`). This is not a newly introduced defect: the previous `update_put` logic also set `alias_level` and `visible` before checking `group.automatic`, meaning those fields were already mutable for automatic groups. The added spec explicitly expects `visible` to change on an automatic group, indicating this behavior is intentional. Therefore the finding is a misread (it’s not a verifiable problem in the diff).

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:115 — "cannot remove members from automatic groups" issues `xhr :put` but the route is `delete members` (PUT maps to add_members), so it only passes because controller specs bypass verb routing and the real DELETE-on-automatic path stays untested.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show a mismatch between routing and the (new) controller spec: `config/routes.rb` wires `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` while the spec example is written as `xhr :put, :remove_member, ...`. However, the proposed finding’s core claim (“PUT maps to add_members, so the test only passes because controller specs bypass verb routing and the real DELETE path stays untested”) is not accurate for Rails controller specs: `xhr :put, :remove_member` directly invokes the `remove_member` action and does not get rerouted to `add_members`. Also, `remove_member` has no verb-dependent branching, so testing it via PUT vs DELETE doesn’t leave a different code path untested. This is at most a test verb inconsistency, not a demonstrated real defect in behavior introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:19 — members` changed response shape (bare array -> {members, meta}), default limit (unlimited for non-automatic -> 50) and pagination, yet the PR adds no spec for it and no spec/controllers/groups_controller_spec.rb exists in the repo.

spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:51 — .update` only covers the automatic-group rename-is-ignored case; deleting `group.name = params[:name]` (line 40) or the `alias_level` assignment (line 37) would leave the whole suite green.

adjudication.rationale: The updated spec suite adds only one test under `context ".update"`: it verifies that for an *automatic* group (id 1) a submitted `name` is ignored while `visible` updates. There is no test asserting that `alias_level` is persisted on update, nor any test asserting that a *non-automatic* group can be renamed via `update`. Therefore, removing the `group.alias_level = ...` line would not fail any spec, and removing the `group.name = params[:name] if ... !group.automatic` line would still keep the automatic-group test passing (since the name would remain unchanged anyway). This is a real, verifiable gap in test coverage introduced/left by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:57 — group.visible.should == true` is a tautology because `visible` defaults to true, so the visible assignment (and the regression where a PUT without `visible` silently sets it false) is not actually verified.

spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:52 — Hardcoded `id: 1` relies on a seeded automatic group existing with that exact id; nothing in the spec establishes group 1 exists or is automatic, so the test is brittle and unreadable.

adjudication.rationale: The updated specs introduce requests like `xhr :put, :update, id: 1, ...` and `xhr :put, :add_members, group_id: 1, ...` to exercise behavior on “automatic groups”, but in the diff there is no setup (e.g., Fabricate/create) that ensures a group with id 1 exists or that it is automatic. That makes these tests dependent on implicit seeded data/ID ordering and therefore brittle/unreadable relative to self-contained spec setup.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:94 — group_id: 1` (and :115) depends on seed data instead of `Fabricate(:group, automatic: true)`, and asserting only status 422 does not distinguish `can_not_modify_automatic` from a generic `render_json_error` 422.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In the updated specs, multiple examples hard-code an ID of `1` for an automatic group (e.g. `xhr :put, :add_members, group_id: 1, ...` and `xhr :put, :update, id: 1, ...`). Nothing in the diff fabricates or creates a group with `id == 1`, so these tests implicitly depend on pre-existing/seeded automatic groups having that specific ID. That is a real, verifiable brittleness/correctness issue in the diff: the tests will fail or behave differently if the test DB doesn’t have the expected seeded group IDs. The additional point about only asserting `422` is also accurate as a weakness (it doesn’t validate the specific error payload), but the hard-coded seed dependency alone is sufficient to be a real problem.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:103 — No test that `add_members` silently skips unknown or whitespace-padded usernames (the deleted "succeeds silently when adding non-existent users" case), so partial-failure behavior is unspecified and unreported.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the prior PATCH-based spec coverage for “succeeds silently when adding non-existent users,” and the new specs for the new `add_members` endpoint do not add an equivalent test. However, that is a test coverage gap, not a verifiable defect introduced by the code itself. The new implementation of `add_members` in `Admin::GroupsController` already silently skips unknown usernames via `if user = User.find_by_username(username)`; whitespace-padded usernames would also simply not match and be skipped. The finding points to missing tests/unspecified behavior rather than a concrete bug/security/correctness issue in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:119 — No test for removing a non-member or unknown `user_id`; `group.users.delete(id)` does a scoped `find` and raises RecordNotFound (404) where the deleted "succeeds silently when removing non-members" spec asserted success.

spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:129 — Assertion uses the live query `group.users.count` and never checks `group.user_count`; the has_many :through `delete` skips join callbacks, so a stale counter cache (which the new pagination UI relies on) passes undetected.

spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:36 — .create` asserts only the stripped name; `visible` handling (absent param makes every new group invisible) and the `render_json_error` branch for an invalid name have no coverage.

app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22 — No test for limit/offset edge values: non-numeric limit becomes 0 (empty page), negative offset reaches Postgres as an error, and there is no upper clamp on limit.

adjudication.rationale: In app/controllers/groups_controller.rb#members the new pagination params are parsed as `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i`. In Ruby, non-numeric strings (e.g. "abc") become 0 via `to_i`, which would yield `limit=0` (empty page). Negative strings (e.g. "-10") become -10, and the code passes that directly into `group.users...limit(limit).offset(offset)`, which can produce SQL like `OFFSET -10` that PostgreSQL rejects. There is also no upper bound/clamp on `limit`, allowing very large limits. These edge cases are not handled anywhere in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:11 — New pagination computed properties ship with no JS unit or acceptance test; `totalPages` is off by one for exact multiples (50 members at limit 50 renders "1/2").

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `totalPages` in `admin-group.js.es6` as `Math.floor(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit")) + 1`. For `user_count` exactly divisible by `limit` (e.g., 50/50), this returns 2 instead of 1, so the UI can show `1/2` when there is only one page. That is a concrete off-by-one bug present in the added code. The comment about missing JS tests is not a functional defect, but it is true that the diff adds pagination behavior without adding any JS tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/group/members.hbs:6 — Public group members page now silently truncates to the first 50 members with no pagination controls and no acceptance test covering the regression.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff changes `GroupsController#members` to always apply `limit = (params[:limit] || 50)` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i`, returning only a page of members plus meta. On the public group members route (`app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6`), `setupController` now sets `controller.model = model` (the Group) and calls `model.findMembers()`, but no UI/actions are added to change `offset`/`limit` for pagination. The template `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/group/members.hbs` now iterates `{{#each m in members}}`, which will only be the `members` property set by `findMembers` (first 50 by default). There are also no new acceptance tests in the diff to cover pagination/regression.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:83 — The refresh_automatic_groups spec stubs `Group.refresh_automatic_groups!` and asserts only that the mock was called plus a 200, verifying the mock rather than any real behavior.

adjudication.rationale: In the updated spec under `context ".refresh_automatic_groups"`, the test does stub/expect `Group.refresh_automatic_groups!` and only asserts a 200 response. However, the controller action `refresh_automatic_groups` itself does nothing beyond calling that class method and returning `success_json`, so verifying the call + 200 is exactly verifying the real behavior of this endpoint. This is more a test-depth/style critique than a verifiable defect or bug introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:105 — response.should be_success` accepts any 2xx and ignores the JSON body, weaker than the `response.status.should == 200` assertions it replaced (same at :127).

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change some specs from `response.status.should == 200` to `response.should be_success` (e.g., in the new `.add_members` spec). While it’s true that `be_success` is less strict (it allows any 2xx), this is a test-strength/style concern rather than a clear defect: the tests still verify the important behavior (e.g., members were added) and the controller actions are intended to return a successful response. The finding doesn’t point to an actual functional bug or failing behavior introduced by the diff, just a weaker assertion preference.
